subject: ContractFlows licensing options & Redwood renewal alignment
messages:
From: Alex Marino <alex@contractflows.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: ContractFlows licensing options & Redwood renewal alignment

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking a minute to connect earlier. ContractFlows builds a combined e-sign + lightweight CLM product that a number of scale-ups use to replace single-purpose e-sign vendors. I attached a short pricing sheet and a draft SOW showing our typical migration assistance and onboarding plan.

Quick highlights:
- Licensing: seat-based, consumption-based, or hybrid — we can model to match your current DocuSign commit.
- Migration: 2-week pilot + automated mapping for existing templates, plus one week of dedicated migration hours.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II, customer-managed KMS, and optional VPC connector for private deployments.

I attached the files (see list below). Is Aug 17 at 3pm PT a good time to walk through pricing and the SLA language?

Thanks,
Alex Marino
Account Executive | ContractFlows
alex@contractflows.com
Attachments: ContractFlows-SOW-draft.pdf (pdf), CF-pricing-Q3-2027.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Marino <alex@contractflows.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: ContractFlows licensing options & Redwood renewal alignment

Alex —

Thanks for the materials. Quick asks so we can prioritize internally before the 8/17 sync:
1) Can you provide a one-page comparison to DocuSign and Ironclad on: licensing model, migration effort (hours), and feature parity for template automation?
2) Confirm KMS options and whether keys remain under customer control for e-signed artifacts.
3) Any data residency guarantees (we have EU and US tenants).
4) Please share a redlineable sample contract (.docx) — our legal team prefers docx for quick editing.

We are in the middle of a renewal conversation and want to see if switching or consolidating makes economic sense. I can do Aug 17 15:00 PT — inviting Marissa and Markus to the call to cover legal/finance.

Olga
Head of Procurement | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Olga, team —

Attaching the comparison and a docx sample of our standard MSA so Marissa can redline. High level:
- Doc comparison: seat vs consumption models mapped; we included migration hours and an estimated 4-week cutover for your size.
- Keys: we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for stored artifacts and offer an HSM-backed option for signing keys.
- Residency: we can route signer artifacts to US/EU tenants — list of regions in the pricing sheet.

Attachments: ContractFlows-SOW-draft.pdf, CF-pricing-Q3-2027.xlsx, ContractFlows-Standard-MSA.docx

If helpful, Samantha (cc'd) can run a short delta demo focused on template automation and API parity. Otherwise, we'll plan to meet 8/17 15:00 PT.

—Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, alex@contractflows.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-12T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: ContractFlows licensing options & Redwood renewal alignment

Alex —

Thanks for the sample MSA and SOW. A couple of legal items we need addressed before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Liability cap — standard for Redwood is 6 months of fees; ContractFlows draft currently shows 12 months. Please confirm you can move to 6 months or provide rationale for a higher cap.
2) Data segregation — because we run multiple tenants (US/EU), we need contractual guarantees that EU tenant data remains within EU controls plus an appendix specifying boundary controls.
3) Audit evidence — please attach latest SOC 2 Type II report and your pen test summary (redacted if needed).
4) Subprocessor list and a Standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with SCCs if data is processed in EU jurisdictions.

Please provide a docx redline; I'll circulate internally. If you can proactively note the specific clauses we've flagged, it speeds our review.

Marissa Cole
Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Alex / Olga —

Thanks for the materials and the clarifications so far. From a finance perspective we are comfortable running a three-week procurement cadence provided we get:
- A fully itemized cost table that shows monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go, and the associated migration professional services fees.
- A discount schedule tied to annual committed volume and a clear true-up mechanism at quarter end.
- Confirmation of any one-time cutover credits or implementation discounts (we will evaluate full TCO vs our current DocuSign/Ironclad spend).

Please share the itemized table and updated MSA redline by EOD Friday (2027-08-20) so we can finalize internal approvals by 8/31.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP Finance | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
